feature_candidates.description: One-hot or embedding of tab_ID added to the scoring function as an additive bias term (implementable in BPR or group_softmax as a per-tab scalar).
feature_candidates.expected_impact: Moderate-high; directly models tab-level long_view rate differences (e.g., tab 4 at 48.93% vs tab 0 at 4.22% in train).
feature_candidates.implementation_scope: Extend src.models.features to include tab_ID embedding; join training rows to tab distribution; no extra data files needed.
feature_candidates.leakage_risk: Low; tab is observed at exposure time and is not a future aggregate.
feature_candidates.name: tab_onehot_bias

feature_candidates.description: Log-binned video duration (e.g., 5–10 buckets) plus a binary indicator for duration==0, concatenated with item embedding.
feature_candidates.expected_impact: Small-to-moderate; zero-duration videos (24k rows) may need dedicated handling to avoid malformed duration arithmetic.
feature_candidates.implementation_scope: Transform video feature table column 'duration' into bucket IDs; add missing indicator; include in candidate set for history_features family.
feature_candidates.leakage_risk: Low; duration is a static video attribute, no temporal aggregation.
feature_candidates.name: duration_bucket_zero_indicator

feature_candidates.description: For each train row, count of user's long_views in the last K older exposures (e.g., last 20 or 50 interactions) before that row, optionally normalized by total prior exposures.
feature_candidates.expected_impact: Moderate-high for nDCG@5; captures short-term user interest drift that static user terms cannot.
feature_candidates.implementation_scope: Sort train rows by user_id, timestamp (hourmin); compute rolling counts per user; cache as a precomputed feature column.
feature_candidates.leakage_risk: Low if strictly past-only; must ensure no future/full-period aggregation is used (no video stats table).
feature_candidates.name: recency_weighted_prior_longview_per_user

findings.evidence: DATA CARD Tab Breakdown (train): per-tab click and long_view rates range from ~0% to ~61% click and ~0% to ~49% long_view.
findings.implication: Adding a tab embedding/bias term may capture large conditional mean differences that item-only features miss, likely recovers a meaningful slice of within-user ranking signal.
findings.observation: In train, tab 4 has 61.96% click and 48.93% long_view, tab 1 has 52.97% click and 38.61% long_view, while tabs 0,6,8,11,14 are far lower; tab distribution is heavily imbalanced (tab 1 73.16% of rows).
findings.title: Tab-specific engagement is strong

findings.evidence: DATA CARD Data Quality: '239 videos with zero duration (24,076 train rows affected)'.
findings.implication: Binning duration into coarse log-spaced buckets plus a separate missing/zero indicator may prevent the model from conflating missingness with real short-form content.
findings.observation: 239 videos have zero duration affecting 24,076 train rows; if duration is treated as a normal numeric feature, they may bias learned item embeddings.
findings.title: Zero-duration videos are a distinct subpopulation

findings.evidence: DATA CARD 'Measured Dead Ends': static user terms have zero intra-group effect; training log allows timestamp-ordered per-user history construction.
findings.implication: The key gains likely come from user×item context, e.g., recency-weighted prior long_view/click within the same tab or category, which can be built strictly from the training log.
findings.observation: First-order user-only terms contribute zero to within-user ranking, as do static features (primary stays at ~0.5950 for 5-feature default); history signals are per-interaction and can vary within a user's ranked list.
findings.title: User history aggregates are the most feasible leakage-safe differentiation

expected_artifacts: A compact EDA table summarizing long_view rate by tab, duration bin, and user_active_degree (train only).
A feature importance report from a quick baseline model (e.g., logistic regression on few features) to rank candidate features.
A correlation matrix between new candidate features and long_view, with leakage flags noted.
A short summary of which candidate features are implementable within bpr/group_softmax/history_features families and their expected impact.
feature_hypotheses: Tab-specific bias terms (e.g., one-hot or embedding for tab_ID) as features will improve ranking, especially for tab 1 and tab 4 where engagement is high and distinct.
Video duration normalized by user's average watched duration or binned into log-scale could capture attention differences; zero-duration videos should be treated as missing with a learned indicator.
User history aggregates over video categories (e.g., average long_view/click ratio per category) will provide informative user-level preferences for ranking.
Recency-weighted user interaction counts (e.g., number of long_views in the last N exposures) could capture short-term drift and improve nDCG@5.
leakage_risks: Video statistics table is a period aggregate over full-platform traffic (ratio ~4892:1 to logged exposures); using it directly could leak unseen exposure data and inflate metrics.
Aggregating user history across the entire training period may inadvertently use future interactions relative to a given train row, causing temporal leakage if not strictly applied per user-time.
Zero-duration videos (239 videos, ~24k train rows) may have special handling but treating them as normal could mislead model if missingness is informative.
Row-order tie-breaking in stable sort means any feature that produces ties may affect nDCG@5; features with many ties should be avoided or randomized.
plan.objective: Plan one leakage-safe EDA pass to uncover tab-specific engagement patterns, duration effects, and user history signals that can be turned into features for the bpr, group_softmax, history_features, or multi_task ranking families, without altering the official evaluator or split.
questions: How does long_view rate vary across tabs after controlling for user, and does tab-specific bias explain variance beyond item features?
Do videos with zero duration systematically differ in long_view rate, and does the interaction between duration and other features improve ranking?
Which user history features (e.g., prior long_view, click, like rates per video category or tab) have the strongest predictive signal for future long_view?
Is there a meaningful within-user temporal pattern (e.g., time-of-day or session position) that correlates with long_view, beyond simple item features?
required_inputs: training log with user_id, video_id, tab, timestamp, and label columns (long_view, is_click)
video feature table (duration, category, upload_type, etc.) with user feature table (active_degree, etc.)
user interaction history derived from the training log only (no test or validation leakage)
existing baseline embedding/feature configuration to compare against

report.recommended_next_focus: Implement a tab embedding baseline (BPR) and a leakage-safe recency-weighted prior long_view feature to test whether either lifts primary above 0.6016; verify no temporal leakage by using only past exposures per user.
report.summary: EDA plan scoped to training-only evidence: tab, duration, and per-user history signals for within-user long_view ranking, with explicit leakage caveats around the full-platform video statistics table and temporal history aggregation.
ui_notes: Show train tab-rate table prominently; tab 4/1 vs tab 0/6 difference is the clearest single-variable signal.
Flag video statistics table as leaky (ratio ~4892:1) and exclude it from the next exploration round.
Monitor nDCG@5 tie effects: tab/duration buckets introduce ties; consider tie-aware evaluation or add small random noise to break stable-sort ties.
